note: Config Override Inspector (COI) reads the #config['key'] hints added by config_override_core_fields, splits config.object:key, and calls Config::hasOverrides(). All behavior comes from one config object coi.settings: override_behavior (disable|noaccess|''), message.enabled/template, overridden_value.enabled/element/secrets, styling.selectors/default. Shipped defaults: override_behavior=disable, message.enabled=true, message.template='This field is overridden by environment specific configuration.', overridden_value.enabled=true, element=true, secrets=false, styling.selectors=true, default=true. Configure route coi.settings (/admin/config/user-interface/coi); permission 'administer config override inspector'. Medium cases read a seeded coi.settings value; hard cases change coi.settings and verify on the live config. coi.settings is owned by this module, so cases mutate and restore only its own config.

evals.prompt: In Config Override Inspector (COI), the override_behavior setting controls what happens to a config form field whose value is overridden. What are its possible values and what does each one do?
evals.expected_output: override_behavior in coi.settings is 'disable' (default; disable the element and optionally show the overridden value as its default), 'noaccess' (hide the element via #access=FALSE), or '' (none; only add CSS classes / a message, don't disable or hide).

evals.prompt: How does COI decide that a configuration form field is overridden, what does it rely on to know which config each field edits, and what does it do to an overridden field by default?
evals.expected_output: COI reads the #config['key'] (or #config_data_store['key']) hint added by config_override_core_fields, splits config.object:key, and calls Config::hasOverrides(key). When true, by default (override_behavior=disable) it disables the field and can inject the overridden value, plus adds config--overridden classes and an override message.

evals.prompt: Inspect the live COI configuration on this site and state the current value of the override_behavior setting.
evals.expected_output: coi.settings override_behavior is currently 'noaccess' (drush config:get coi.settings override_behavior).

evals.prompt: COI shows a message next to overridden config fields. Inspect the live coi.settings configuration and report the exact override message template currently configured.
evals.expected_output: coi.settings message.template is currently 'COI known override message' (from coi.settings; message.enabled controls whether it is shown).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure Config Override Inspector so that overridden config form fields are HIDDEN (no access) rather than merely disabled. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: coi.settings override_behavior is set to 'noaccess' (e.g. drush config:set coi.settings override_behavior noaccess), which makes overridden fields get #access=FALSE.

evals.prompt: Configure Config Override Inspector so that overridden values on fields marked as secret are exposed (shown) rather than masked. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: coi.settings overridden_value.secrets is set to true (e.g. drush config:set coi.settings overridden_value.secrets 1), so COI shows overridden values even for secret-marked elements.
